items.title: Lenders tighten credit as rate hikes shrink refi market
items.description: Originations Lenders tighten credit as rate hikes shrink refi market By Brad Finkelstein CloseText About Brad twitter nmnbrad mailto bradley.finkelstein@arizent.com linkedin brad-finkelstein-8b2b9a5/ Published October 08, 2026, 3:51 p.m. EDT | Updated October 08, 2026, 8:52 p.m. EDT 2 Min Read Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Key Insight: Find out how lenders adjusted credit access as conforming mortgage rates rose in September. What's at Stake: Homebuyers and refinancers facing restricted access to key loan programs as lenders pull back. Expert Quote: "Growth in non-agency loan programs continues to support this segment." — Joel Kan, MBA Overview bullets generated by AI with editorial review. Mortgage program availability tightened in September, as conventional lenders reacted to an environment where conforming mortgage rates rose 64 basis points. Processing Content It is the fourth month out of the last six where lenders cut back on the type of credit they were extending to homebuyers and refinancers. The Mortgage Bankers Association's Mortgage Credit Availability Index ended last month at 107.1, a 0.2% decline from August's 107.3. For September 2025 , the index was at 104.4. The index baseline is 100, measuring credit availability in March 2012. Since February 2025, the MCAI has been higher than this level and over 104 since August of that year. This month's change came entirely from the conventional component, with the conforming index down by 0.2% and the jumbo down 0.5%, even with a rate inversion. Rates on the conforming 30-year fixed were 7.49% the week ended Oct. 2 compared with 6.85% on Sept. 4, the MBA's Weekly Application Survey noted. Jumbo program tightening occurred as its rate went to 7.39% at the end of September from 6.74%. "Lenders tightened documentation requirements on conventional loans and reduced offerings of loans that allow for cash-out refinances and investor home purchases," said Joel Kan, the MBA's vice president and deputy chief economist in a press release. "However, recent growth in non-agency loan programs continues to support this segment of the market." Adjustable-rate mortgage application volume was at 10.3%, unchanged from the prior week, the WAS reported. Rates on the 5/1 ARM declined to 6.43% from 6.47%. Refinance applications declined 8% from the prior week; they were 56% lower from the same time in 2025. Purchases were just 2% lower week-to-week and down 15% compared with one year prior. While securitization activity lags mortgage originations, September had just over $16 billion in priced residential mortgage-backed securities issuances according to Morningstar DBRS, citing CreditFlow data. This was 86% of the 2026 monthly average of $21.4 billion. "still in context with the highest monthly volumes seen last year," the report said. "To close out Q3 2026, pricing volume totaled approximately $61 billion, the lowest quarter of the year so far, but not by much, as Q3 volume was higher than any quarter of 2025." Non-qualified mortgages made up 45% of the monthly volume, which is around the average of new issuance for this type. Prime jumbo was 17% and second lien products , 13.9%. "September's RMBS performance data reflects a market adjusting to persistently higher interest rates ," said Mark Fontanilla, senior vice president, U.S. RMBS ratings at Morningstar DBRS, in a press release. Delinquencies were higher and prepayment speeds continued to slow. "Despite those pressures, deal structures remained largely stable, credit losses stayed low, and credit enhancement levels continued to improve," Fontanilla said. "At the same time, issuance activity remained robust, with year-to-date RMBS volume already surpassing last year's full-year total and reaching a post-Global Financial Crisis record." items.title: HUD outlines 7 steps to update manufactured housing code
items.description: In July, the manufactured housing industry secured a major policy win — the removal of the permanent chassis requirement — following the passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act . Industry leaders argue the change will help manufactured housing gain greater acceptance in higher-density suburban, urban and infill markets, and better support the construction of multi-story homes. However, they acknowledge that it could take at least a year, if not more, to begin realizing those benefits, as the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) must first implement any changes to the manufactured housing HUD code before manufacturers can begin selling homes without a permanent chassis. On Wednesday, HUD offered its first indication that it has begun that implementation process, with the release of its “ Next Generation Manufactured Housing Action Plan .” HUD’s plan details seven actions to modernize and improve the manufactured housing code, and ensure that the code is in compliance with the guidelines established under the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. Though the agency hasn’t said when implementation will wrap up, releasing the plan is a sign that the work is underway. “The overarching goal is straightforward: preserve the strengths of the federal manufactured housing system while ensuring that it can support innovation and the next generation of factory-built housing,” the document read. The seven actions in HUD’s plan 1. Update manufactured housing energy efficiency standards HUD will conduct rulemaking to update 24 CFR Part 3280 energy efficiency standards for manufactured housing, as required by the 21st Century Road to Housing Act. 2. Update HUD code for chassis-free construction HUD will revise the Manufactured Home Construction and Safety Standards in 24 CFR Part 3280 to accommodate homes built without a permanent chassis. This will include standards for structural design, transportation, lifting, connections and related technical requirements. The goal is to establish a clear framework for homes built with and without a permanent chassis that allows flexibility for new designs. 3. Update 24 CFR Part 3285 for foundations and installation HUD will update the Model Manufactured Home Installation Standards in 24 CFR Part 3285 to address how chassis-free homes are supported and attached to the ground. HUD’s Manufactured Housing Consensus Committee will recommend changes related to foundations, anchoring, structural connections, setting procedures and other installation requirements. The update is intended to allow a range of support systems and new designs while ensuring safe and reliable performance. 4. Establish a multi-module construction pathway HUD plans to create more flexible pathways for multi-module construction, accounting for situations where a home is built in multiple factory-made sections. With the chassis requirement removed, HUD will explore how these transportable sections can be designed, transported, assembled and completed on-site while preserving substantial factory completion. The end goal is expanding the range of housing types and designs that manufacturers can deliver. 5. Develop a performance-based code for buildings with five or more units HUD will develop a performance-based federal construction and safety code, modeled on Part 3280, for residential structures containing five or more units. The plan notes that larger buildings introduce issues such as common corridors, stairs, accessibility, fire separation, shared systems and egress that are not fully addressed in the current standards. A performance-based code for five-plus-unit buildings would establish a national pathway for repeatable multifamily construction under a federal framework. In accordance with this plan, HUD selected the National Institute of Building Sciences to support an initiative aimed at expanding the use of factory-built construction for multifamily housing. items.title: Problem loans: Tracking the biggest multifamily delinquencies
items.description: An article from Tracker Problem loans: Tracking the biggest multifamily delinquencies Properties recently fell into distress in Missouri, Tennessee, New York and Texas. Published Oct. 8, 2026 • Updated June 17, 2026 By Leslie Shaver Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print Add us on Google Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print Add us on Google Multifamily Dive is tracking the problem loans that have come to light since January 2023. Getty Images Apartment distress showed mixed signals through the summer and into the fall of 2026. Freddie Mac s delinquency rate for multifamily loans rose from 0.48% in August 2025 to 0.64% in August 2026, its highest level in 20 years , according to Mortgage Point. Fannie Mae s rate fell from 0.68% in August 2025 to 0.57% in August 2026. Delinquencies on bank-held multifamily loans improved to 1.41% in Q2 2026, down from a multiyear high of 1.47% in Q1, according to a CRED iQ analysis of FDIC data from all insured institutions. Beneath the data is market sentiment, which isn t as opaque. Multifamily investors say that banks are finally getting aggressive with borrowers and resolving issues with troubled properties. Shimon Greenspan, CFO of Long Beach, California-based apartment owner Westland Real Estate Group, told Multifamily Dive that lenders initially allowed borrowers to extend and pretend. But since July, he said more people have realized interest rates won t come down soon enough to rescue owners. I think we re going to start to see a lot of that stuff work out in ways that it hadn t previously been forced to work out, Greenspan said. As that happens, Gaia Real Estate co-founder and CEO Danny Fishman thinks debt funds may be less likely to bail out troubled borrowers. I think we are starting to see more distress in the industry, he said. Those [debt] funds saved them and basically they were kicking the can another year too. And I think that comes to an end. As properties, particularly those with CMBS loans, face issues, Multifamily Dive continues to monitor the situation. Here is a look at some properties that faced issues over the summer. items.title: Deutsche Bank Files $260M Foreclosure Suit For Broward County Mall
items.description: Deutsche Bank Files $260M Foreclosure Suit For Broward County Mall October 8, 2026 | 4:02 pm ET Chloe Gallivan, South Florida New York-based BGRE has been able to rebrand from its previous name, Brookfield Properties , but it hasn't been able to shake financial pressures on a $260M mortgage tied to a Broward County mall after years of cash flow and occupancy struggles. Google Maps Pembroke Lakes Mall at 11401 Pines Blvd. in Pembroke Pines Deutsche Bank National Trust Co. filed a foreclosure suit against Pembroke Lakes Mall LLC on behalf of a commercial mortgage-backed securities trust for Goldman Sachs , claiming that it failed to repay its mortgage by its maturity date in March last year, according to the suit filed in the Broward County Circuit Court. BGRE and Deutsche did not respond to requests for comment. Polsinelli attorney Marx Calderón, who represents Deutsche in the filing, also did not respond to a request for comment. Deutsche said the borrower was notified of the default in April 2025 and again in April 2026 and owes a total of $263.8M as of Sept. 1, including principal, interest and default interest. The Germany-based bank also asked the court to appoint Carmen Spinoso of Spinoso Real Estate Group as receiver of the property, according to the filings. BGRE had requested a three-year loan extension, but it was not approved, according to Kroll Bond Rating Agency . About 535K SF of the 1M SF Pembroke Lakes Mall serves as collateral for the loan. The property was last appraised in April this year at $112M — a 73% decrease from the $427M appraised value at closing in 2013, when Goldman Sachs originated the loan, according to KBRA . BGRE obtained the mall at 11401 Pines Blvd. in 2018 when it acquired shopping mall REIT General Growth Properties. The mall really started to struggle coming out of the pandemic. Occupancy dropped from 100% to 84% in 2022, The Real Deal reported at the time , citing a Morningstar report. Even while occupancy at Pembroke Lakes climbed back to 95% in September 2024, cash flow had declined 30%, according to Morningstar. The loan was transferred into special servicing in April last year. Pembroke Lakes was built in 1992 and renovated in 2006. Tenants include H M, American Eagle, AMC Theatres and Dillard's, according to its website. Despite mall values climbing 13% year-over-year nationwide, as The Wall Street Journal reported , Pembroke Lakes is among many malls across the country saddled with debt and growing distress. Of the 423 CMBS loans totaling $42B that Morningstar tracks attached to 182 malls, 92 loans totaling $8.7B are in special servicing, and 42 loans totaling $3.4B are delinquent. items.title: NYC Is Building Hotels Again. It May Not Be Enough
items.description: NYC Is Building Hotels Again. It May Not Be Enough October 8, 2026 | 6:48 pm ET Ciara Long, New York City A Sixth Avenue lot just off Times Square has been home to a magazine building and a pop-up shopping court, and outlasted its owner’s decision to abandon plans for a luxury hotel there. Last month, construction signs on its plywood fence announced what’s next: a 41-story hotel, due in 2029. It’s one of the last hotel projects to win approval before the city made new ones far harder to build. Google Maps 1146-1150 Sixth Ave., one of three new Midtown Manhattan hotels under development New York City’s hotel construction pipeline is about a third of what it was in 2020, according to an October report from the New York State Comptroller’s Office . The city's hotels have the highest occupancy in the country, and tourism is nearly back to pre-pandemic levels. New York will easily absorb what’s coming, industry figures say, and may soon run short. Visitor numbers will likely top their 2019 record by 2028, if not next year, said Vijay Dandapani, president and CEO of the Hotel Association of New York City . "At that point, we’re going to be under-hoteled, meaning there won’t be enough hotels," he said. New York City’s hotels have had a strong year. Occupancy in most Manhattan submarkets has topped 80% so far in 2026, CoStar Group Director of Hospitality Market Analytics Didio Pequeno told Bisnow . Nationally, hotel occupancy was 66.4% in August, according to CoStar data . The city has 24 hotel projects totaling 5,778 rooms in active development through 2028, according to New York City Tourism + Conventions, the city’s tourism marketing agency. That much new supply might strain other hotel markets, Pequeno said. “Usually, that's a short-term shock to the system,” he said. “Over time, performance does pick up, especially in a place like New York, where demand and occupancy levels are so high.” And demand is still growing. The city drew 65 million visitors last year, just shy of its 2019 record , and the agency expects that number to climb to 66.3 million this year. The Sixth Avenue tower joins two larger hotel projects already rising nearby in Midtown. Renderings released this month show a 41-story tower at 1146-1150 Sixth Ave., wrapped in reflective glass framed by copper-toned panels and designed by Stonehill Taylor. Permits issued in 2021 called for 310 rooms. Fortuna Realty Group, the firm founded by Morris Moinian, bought the site, then home to the eight-story Pan American Magazine Building, for $39M in 2012, public records show . Moinian, the younger brother of Moinian Group founder Joseph Moinian, shelved the hotel plan in 2020 and tried to sell the property, according to the New York Post . About 10 blocks north, at Broadway and West 54th Street, family-owned Spanish chain RIU Hotels Resorts is building its third New York City hotel — a 54-story tower with 673 rooms and two 300-seat restaurants, due in 2027. Google Maps 1710 Broadway under construction in April 2026 Extell Development sold the site to RIU for $172.8M in 2023, according to PincusCo , roughly $95M less than the $268M it paid in 2017 for the property and 360K SF of air rights, according to New York YIMBY . The tower is expected to top out this year, YIMBY reported. Extell, meanwhile, is building its own hotel about eight blocks south. The Torch , at 740 Eighth Ave. between West 45th and 46th streets, had risen 40 stories as of September, The Real Deal reported . The Gary Barnett -led firm is building a 1,800-key hotel an avenue west of the Times Square bow tie, according to The Real Deal , topped by an observation deck and a 260-foot drop ride . Midtown hotels are well positioned to absorb the new rooms, Dandapani and Pequeno said. items.title: Downtown Los Angeles Retail, Office Hub The Bloc Up For Sale
items.description: Downtown Los Angeles Retail, Office Hub The Bloc Up For Sale October 8, 2026 | 3:45 pm ET Bianca Barragán, Southern California Courtesy of National Real Estate Advisors The Bloc takes up an actual city block in Downtown LA. A city block-sized retail and office development in Downtown Los Angeles has hit the market. Its sale will say a lot about demand for these uses in DTLA. National Real Estate Advisors is selling The Bloc , which features 420K SF of retail including apparel retailer Uniqlo and an Alamo Drafthouse , 730K SF of Class-A office space in a 33-story tower, and a parking structure with nearly 2,000 stalls. “Now that sales transactions are once again becoming the norm in Downtown LA and closed sales are establishing clear price points, buyers can finally underwrite against defensible and quantifiable market evidence,” Cushman Wakefield Executive Vice Chairman Mike Condon said in a statement. Condon and Vice Chairman Kevin Donner are marketing the property for the owner, National Real Estate Advisors. Condon told the Los Angeles Times that the vacant Macy's building presented an advantage for potential buyers. “That vacancy is where a lot of the value for the project will be derived,” he told the Times. “That’s the big opportunity.” The Bloc is a Downtown mainstay. It was renovated in the aughts in a process that removed its roof, added more restaurants along the perimeter, and made it an open-air shopping center that hosts events on a central lawn. The developer behind the changes, Wayne Ratkovich of Ratkovich Co ., sold his stake in the property to his partner, NREA, in 2018 for an undisclosed amount. “The Bloc is now positioned to become a highly successful investment and an epicenter for DTLA’s revitalization,” said Jeff Kanne , president and CEO of National Real Estate Advisors, in a statement at the time. Downtown's upward trajectory was knocked off course by the pandemic, and the neighborhood is still working to rebound. As other submarkets around the city have regained their footing, Downtown is, for many investors and owners, still viewed as a challenged market . The team selling the Bloc says the tide is turning. “We're seeing capital come back to Downtown LA — not just opportunistic, bargain hunting buyers, but owner-users, public agencies, and long-term institutional and high net worth holders who look to execute a typical value add business plan," Condon said in a statement. "That's a meaningfully different buyer pool than we saw even twelve months ago.” A real estate source estimated that the office and retail portion of the property is worth about $160M, the Los Angeles Times reported . The Bloc's hotel, the Sheraton Grand Los Angeles, is also for sale but is being marketed by a separate team.
